VERS. 12.-- *Fornicatio mulieris.* [n: (RAB.)] Per haec tria curiositatem humanae mentis ostendit, etc., *usque ad* per superbiam vitae, cum adderet, *Eritis sicut dii [n: (Gen. III)]*.

VERS. 16.-- *Ossa illius impinguabit.* Charitate scilicet, unde: *Qui servat mandata mea, ille est qui diligit me, et diligetur a Patre meo, et ego diligam eum [n: (Joan. XIV)]*.

[1212C]VERS. 18.-- *Mulier,* etc. Quia sapientia Dei animas electorum imbuit, et tribuit eis custodiam oris et efficaciam operis, nec eos a se declinare permittit, quia omnis qui natus est ex Deo, non peccat, fidem, scilicet violando, vel charitatem: *Quia semen Dei,* id est verbum, quo renatus est, *in se habet.*

VERS. 23.-- *Columnae aureae.* Doctores sapientia fulgentes, super bases argenteas locantur, cum in sancta Scriptura praedicatione sua insigniuntur.

VERS. 25.-- *In duobus.* [n: (RAB.)] Notat sapientia, etc., *usque ad* vel deserto tramite veritatis sequitur devia erroris.

VERS. 28.-- *Difficile exuitur.* [n: (RAB.)] Actus pessimus, non res honesta damnatur. Ille negotiator abominandus, qui per immoderatam ambitionem merces [1212D] suas plus perjurio onerat quam pretio.

## CAPUT XXVII.

VERS. 1.-- *Propter inopiam,* etc., [n: (RAB.)] Sicut in medio. Hic comparatione, etc., *usque ad* et in futuro poena aeterna manet.

VERS. 5.-- *Sicut in percussura cribri.* [n: (ID.)] Sicut cribrum, etc., *usque ad: Satanas expetivit vos, ut cribraret sicut triticum.*

VERS. 7.-- *Sicut rusticatio de ligno.* [n: (ID.)] Unaquaeque arbor, etc., *usque ad* cultura ergo ligni in fructu manifestat qualitatem ejus.

VERS. 8.-- *Ante sermonem.* Quia sermo indicat cogitationem. Quasi dicat: Nemo laudet eum, quem [1213A] manifestis indiciis non cognovit laude dignum. Potest autem sermo pro bono opere accipi, ut neminem ante probationem bonorum operum laudemus. Unde: *Non laudes ante mortem quemquam.*

VERS. 13.-- *In medio.* [n: (RAB.)] Temperantiam et cautelam loquendi docet, etc., *usque ad: Qui autem fecerit et docuerit, hic magnus vocabitur in regno coelorum [n: (Matth. V)]*.

VERS. 15.-- *Loquela,* etc. Quia sicut actio eorum bonis contraria: et loquela ad mala dicendum prona, ad audiendum gravis.

VERS. 17.-- *Qui denudat.* Ostendit in quo maxime laeditur amicitia, in malo, scilicet proditionis, quae fidem, scilicet perdit, nec amicitiae aequitatem custodit, et ideo dissipat charitatem.

[1213B]VERS. 22.-- *Quasi caprea.* Caprea, capra sylvestris, dicta quasi capiens ardua. Capreae autem ibices vel avices dicuntur, eo quod ad instar avium alta et excelsa teneant: et in sublimibus habitent, ita ut de sublimitate vix humanis obtutibus pateant. Hae si quando adversitatem ferarum, vel hominum praesenserint: de altis cacuminibus sese praecipitantes, suis se cornibus in ramis arborum recipiunt illaesas.

VERS. 24.-- *Denudare autem,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] Proditoris inconstantiam morum ostendit, etc., *usque ad: Homo apostata, vir inutilis graditur ore perverso, annuit oculis, terit pede,* etc. [n: (Prov. VI)].

VERS. 30.-- *Facienti nequissimum consilium.* Quia non prospicit quod veniat dies ejus. Aestimat enim [1213C] haereticus vel schismaticus, quod melior sit ejus secta quam veritas catholica: unde illudit seipsum.

## CAPUT XXVIII.

VERS. 8.-- *Memorare.* [n: (RAB.)] Qui Deum timet, iram vel furorem compescit, et non obliviscitur testamenti Dei, qui ait: *Dimittite et dimittetur vobis [n: (Luc. IX)]*.

VERS. 13.-- *Certamen.* Indiscreta actio: unde, *Noli esse nimium justus, neque plus sapias quam necesse est, ne obstupescas.* Disciplina ergo immoderata excitat furoris ardorem, et procax loquela effusionem sanguinis.

VERS. 19.-- *Lingua tertia.* Haeretica doctrina, quae nec Veteri nec Novo Testamento concordat, et [1213D] auditorum corda conturbat, et de gente in gentem pergens, seditionem excitat.

VERS. 21.-- *Plaga autem.* Pejor est interitus animae quam occidunt haeretici, quam quilibet cruciatus corporis.

*Beatus qui tectus.* Beatus, qui non consentit haereticis, et cujus cor eorum eloquentia non subvertit, quia sicut alienus est ab eorum malitia, ita separatur a poena.

VERS. 28.-- *Sepi aures.* Postquam malum linguae extirpavit, ad doctrinam auditoris se convertit.



## CAPUT XXIX.

VERS. 5.-- *Donec accipiant.* [n: (RAB.)] Hujusmodi morbum melius curat timor Dei. Qui enim Deum [1214A] quasi semper praesentem pertimescit, neminem fraudare intendit.

VERS. 10.-- *Multis,* etc. [n: (ID.)] Illos notat, qui neminem laedere volunt, sed prae timore periturarum rerum prodesse nolunt. Contra quos dicitur: *Nolite thesaurizare vobis thesauros in terra [n: (Matth. VI)]*.

VERS. 12.-- *Propter mandatum.* Omnibus indigentibus misericordia est facienda, nec pro avaritia charitas proximi amittenda.

VERS. 13.-- *Et non abscondas.* Qui enim viderit fratrem suum necesse habere, et clauserit viscera sua ab eo, quomodo charitas Dei manet in eo?

VERS. 16, 17, 18.-- *Super scutum potentis,* etc. Magis valet eleemosyna contra jacula inimici, quam [1214B] arma terrena: quia haec dubiam, illa certissimam parit victoriam, ut absorbeatur mors in victoria.

VERS. 23.-- *Qui perdiderit,* etc. Id est, qui unitatem fidei, et sinceritatem legis non custodit, sed implicatur erroribus variis.

VERS. 20.-- *Gratiam fidejussoris,* etc. Doctorem scilicet qui pro fide et bonis operibus promittit vitam aeternam. Haec sententia Pelagium reprehendit qui liberum arbitrium gratiae praeponit, cum per solam gratiam liberentur electi.

VERS. 27.-- *Recupera proximum.* Consulit, ut secundum vires proximo praebeas solatium, et sic tibi praevideas, ne in laqueum cadas.

VERS. 28.-- *Initium vitae,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] Fragilitatem, et hospitalitatem et honestatem docet, etc., [1214C] *usque ad* et Dominus primis parentibus pelliceas tunicas post peccatum fecit.

VERS. 29.-- *Melior est victus pauperis,* etc. Ad litteram. Melius est tenuem victum sub vili tugurio sumere in securitate, quam splendidas epulas cum fatigatione in incertis locis quaerere. [n: (ID.)] Allegorice. Melior est victus, etc., *usque ad* ubi labor et superflua cura.

VERS. 30.-- *Minimum.* [n: (ID.)] Sufficiat tibi quod habes, etc., *usque ad* melius est nomen bonum quam deliciae multae.

VERS. 33.-- *Transi.* Quasi: Qui alieno delectaris hospitio, redi ad propria, et de labore tuo te et alios pasce. Noli de aliena domo pastum tibi superfluum quaerere. Sufficit tibi susceptio proximorum.

[1214D]VERS. 35.-- *Improperium.* [n: (RAB.)] Mystice autem monetur vir ecclesiasticus, etc., *usque ad* in futuro autem examine aeternum confusionis improperium sustineat.

## CAPUT XXX.

VERS. 1.-- *Qui diligit filium.* [n: (RAB.)] Patres tam carnales quam spirituales monet, ut filios suos diligenter erudiant, ut honeste vivant, ne lasciviendo per aliorum dogmata discurrant.

VERS. 8.-- *Equus indomitus.* Equus indomitus in praecipitium vadit; filius indisciplinatus in peccatum ruit. Docet ergo spirituales patres, ut filios suos erudiant et corrigant; ne eis immoderate frena [1215A] relaxent, ne cadant in turpitudinem vitiorum, et ipsi ignominiam sustineant sempiternam.

VERS. 14.-- *Melior est pauper.* Dulcis est somnus operanti, sive multum comedat, sive parum. Saturitas enim divitis non sinit dormire eum.

VERS. 15.-- *Salus animae.* Vera salus animae justitia est, cui aurum et argentum non valent comparari, quia non proderunt divitiae in die ultionis. Justitia autem animam liberabit a morte.

VERS. 18.-- *Bona abscondita.* [n: (RAB.)] Contra eos loquitur, qui talentum verbi abscondunt; quorum scientia virtutibus inutilis, sicut epulae mortuis et thesaurus.

VERS. 21.-- *Sicut spado.* Non facit ad complexum virginis, sic adoratio idoli, adorantibus incongrua [1215B] et inutilis.

VERS. 23.-- *Jucunditas cordis.* Quia nulla virtus sine ea consistit. *Major autem horum est charitas [n: (I Cor. XIII)]*.

VERS. 26.-- *Minuunt dies,* etc. *Viri sanguinum non dimidiabunt dies suos [n: (Psal. LIV)]*. [n: (ID.)] Id est, prosperitatem, quam sibi promittunt, non possunt habere in perpetuum.

## CAPUT XXXI.

VERS. 1.-- *Lignum offensionis.* [n: (RAB.)] Sicut Adam in ligno vetito, etc., *usque ad* quae splendore eloquentiae nitet, et curiosos seducit.

VERS. 12.-- *Supra mensam.* [n: (ID.)] Ad litteram, continentiam, etc., *usque ad* sed sanctorum doctorum [01215C] viam teneamus.

VERS. 13.-- *Non dicas,* etc. [n: (ID.)] Quasi diceret: Ne praesumptione aliquid agas, vel antequam discas ad scribendum manum mittas.

VERS. 19.-- *Utere,* etc. Quasi: Sobrietatem dilige, temperanter age, et ne quid nimis, ne in scandalum confusionis incidas. Convenit ergo Christiano ante omnia humilitatem diligere, in lectione Scripturae cautum esse, rectam fidem tenere, modum in scientia servare, et charitatis regulam, ut probatus sit coram Deo et hominibus.

VERS. 22.-- *Quam sufficiens.* Tenuis victus tam animae quam corpori utilis est, superfluus vero e contra. *Vinum exiguum.* Vinum quoque spirituale [1215D] sumptum moderate, utile est tam corpori quam animae: immoderate enim insanire facit, et a Deo disjungit, unde anxia cura, et turbatio maxima, et perpetua tortura.

VERS. 24.-- *Somnus sanitatis.* Subtilior est somnus in parvo victu. Mystice autem qui sobrius est in spirituali vino, in contemplatione veritatis quiescit usque in mane resurrectionis.

VERS. 25.-- *Et vome,* etc. Aiunt medici, quod vomitus stomachum purgat: choleram minuit. Mystice autem qui transgreditur mensuram et gravatur carnalibus delictis, per confessionem peccati foeditatem evomat, et per corporis castigationem ad sanitatem redeat.

VERS. 27.-- *In omnibus operibus.* Monet ne tempus [1216A] perdamus, bene operemur, ut mandata Dei custodientes requiem inveniamus animabus nostris.

VERS. 28.-- *Splendidum.* Ad litteram: ad eleemosynam invitat: Quia *qui seminat in benedictionibus, de benedictionibus et metet [n: (II Cor. IX)]*. Mystice autem qui panem verbi fideliter dispensat, et testimonium veritatis non occultat, in praesenti, et in futuro benedicetur.

VERS. 30.-- *Multos enim,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] Id est ebrietas multos subvertit, quae sensum minuit, iram excitat, libidinem inflammat, animi secreta revelat.

VERS. 31.-- *Ignis.* Id est sicut ignis ferri duritiam mollit, et candescere facit; sic vinum corda superborum inflammans, ad facinus impellit.

VERS. 32.-- *Aequa vita.* Vinum sobrie potatum [1216B] vitam aequitatis non tollit; sed sobrietatem, et caetera virtutum ornamenta adducit. *Vinum.* Patet irritationem, iram, et ruinas multas ebrietate nasci, et amaritudinem animae, et scelerum vulnera multiplicari.

## CAPUT XXXII.

VERS. 1.-- *Rectorem.* [n: (RAB.)] Qui dignitate praeest, non debet superbire: *Qui major est vestrum, fiat sicut minor,* etc. [n: (Matth. X)].

VERS. 7.-- *Gemmula carbunculi.* [n: (RAB.)] Ardentium gemmarum principatum tenet, etc., *usque ad* et mysteria Dominicae passionis digno veneratur sacramento.

VERS. 14.-- *Ante grandinem.* [n: (ID.)] Fulgor coruscationis praeibit pondus grandinis; sic nitor gratiae [1216C] verecundiam.

VERS. 15.-- *Hora surgenti.* [n: (ID.)] Admonet ne simus tristes, etc., *usque ad* qui per gratiam nos fecit, et bonis [operibus] omnibus replevit.

VERS. 22.-- *Vir consilii.* Quanto quis prudentior, tanto utitur proximorum consilio, ut addat sibi intelligentiam.

VERS. 24.-- *Fili, sine consilio.* Possunt haec de catholico et haeretico accipi. Catholicus enim Deum timens omnia agit doctorum consilio et Scripturarum documento. Haereticus vero propria confidens sapientia, et propriis instat inventionibus: sed cum stultitia ejus apparuerit, per sanctos praedicatores divinis arguetur sententiis



## CAPUT XXXIII.

[1216D]

VERS. 5.-- *Praecordia fatui.* [n: (RAB.)] Sicut rota carri et axis, etc., *usque ad: Cor stultorum dissimile erit [n: (Prov. XV)]*.

VERS. 6.-- *Equus,* etc. [n: (ID.)] Sicut jumento nulla est ratio, etc., *usque ad* sed per oris officia aequaliter utrique pandit secreta.

VERS. 7.-- *Quare dies.* [n: (ID.)] Quia superius stultum vituperavit, etc., *usque ad* ut sint in signa et tempora, et dies, et annos.

VERS. 8.-- *Facto sole.* [n: (ID.)] Praecepit Deus in lege, etc., *usque ad* et maxime placere quod ordine et ratione fit.

VERS. 10.-- *Ex ipsis exaltavit.* [n: (ID.)] Id est, sua [1217A] discretione illos distinxit, quos pro benefactis remuneravit, et quibus pro malefactis dignam mercedem retribuit. *Et omnes homines.* Post dispositionem siderum, etc., *usque ad* impios vero aeterna maledictione damnavit.

VERS. 13.-- *Quasi lutum,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] In manu sua habet conditor massam humani generis, etc., *usque ad* et quem debeat indurare secundum justitiam.

VERS. 15.-- *Contra malum.* Investigator operum Dei invenit in ipsis quamdam contrarietatem, sed mirabiliter a Deo ordinatam. Non est ergo mali conditor Deus, qui fecit omnia bona valde; nec mortem fecit, nec laetatur in perditione mortuorum, sed universitatis est mirabilis ordinator. Naturae ergo bonae sunt, et a Deo sunt: vitia vero non ex Deo.

[1217B]VERS. 18.-- *Respicite.* Omnes communiter admonet, ut juris sui rationem non omittant, quia non aliter potest habere pacem et quietem. Qui enim primatus sui auctoritatem perdit, in despectionem et angustiam se mittit: qui autem locum suum sapienter custodit, se et suos ad profectum virtutis dirigit.

VERS. 19.-- *Audite.* Ad litteram patres docet, ut filios regant, et cum disciplina nutriant, donec veniant ad aetatem perfectam, ut digni haeredes patrum suorum possint esse. Spiritualiter vero instruit rectores Ecclesiae, ut dignitatem suam usque ad finem teneant et discipulos suos bene nutritos haeredes sui laboris relinquant. Tenere debent rectores exterius quod pro aliorum utilitate suscipiunt.

VERS. 25.-- *Cibaria et virga,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] Necesse [1217C] est ut iniqui servi, etc., *usque ad* ut habeant, scilicet victum et vestitum, non vagandi otium.

VERS. 31.-- *Si est tibi fidelis,* etc. [n: (ID.)] Boni servi legem tradidit, etc., *usque ad* non est enim homo persequendus, sed vitia.

## CAPUT XXXIV.

VERS. 2.-- *Quasi qui apprehendit.* [n: (RAB.)] Significat somnia fallacia, etc., *usque ad* ut sciant quid a bono spiritu percipiant, vel quid ab illusione patiantur.

VERS. 8.-- *Sine mendacio.* Abjectis somniis hortatur credendum esse doctrinae sapientiae, quae in ore fidelis viri complantata sine mendacio consummat verbum.

[1217D]VERS. 9.-- *Enarrabit intellectum.* Aliis instruendis: unde, *Benedictus Deus, qui consolatur nos in omni tribulatione nostra, ut possimus consolari eos qui in omni pressura sunt [n: (II Cor. XII)]*.

VERS. 10, 11.-- *Qui autem in multis,* etc. Mutabilis, scilicet mente, instabilis est actione. Vel, qui fidei unitate perdita multiplices sequitur haereticorum sectas, multis impietatibus servit.

VERS. 12.-- *Plurimas verborum* [n: (RAB.)] Scripturam significat; qui intente Scripturam meditatur, et humiliter Dominum deprecatur, et rerum et verborum scientiam adipiscitur.

VERS. 23.-- *Dona iniquorum.* Valde detestabile est sacrificium, quod orbati patris dolori comparatur. [1218A] Quidam pensant quanta tribuunt, et non quanta rapiunt. Et congregant mercedes, et mittunt eas in saccum pertusum. In sacco pertuso videtur, quando pecunia mittitur, sed non quando amittitur. Qui ergo quanta largiuntur aspiciunt, sed non quanta rapiunt, in sacculo pertuso mercedes mittunt, quia eas in spem fiduciae suae intuentes congerunt, sed non se intuentes perdunt.

VERS. 26.-- *Qui aufert.* [n: (RAB.)] In sudore vultus sui pauper acquirit panem. Qui hunc violenter tollit, quasi qui occidit proximum suum.

VERS. 28.-- *Unus aedificans.* Hoc est quod supra dixit, sacrificium de rapina non esse acceptabile. Qui offert de rapina, videtur sibi aedificium virtutum praeparere, non crimen avaritiae attendit et rapinae.

[1218B]VERS. 30.-- *Qui baptizatur.* [n: (ID.)] Lavamini, etc., *usque ad* et rursum flenda committunt.

## CAPUT XXXV.

VERS. 1.-- *Qui conservat.* [n: (RAB.)] Bene orat, etc., *usque ad* quia bene operando servat justitiam.

VERS. 3.-- *Propitiationum.* Inter *litare et sacrificare* hoc distat. Nam sacrificat qui sacrificium facit. Litat qui sacrificium facit, et quod sacrificio petiit, impetrat.

VERS. 4.-- *Retribuet,* etc. Utrumque, scilicet gratum Deo, et quod in altari in commemorationem Jesu Christi offertur, et quod per charitatem proximo tribuitur.

VERS. 10.-- *Bono animo.* [n: (ID.)] Quidquid bono [1218C] animo non datur, apud Deum gratiam non meretur. Homo enim videt in facie, Deus autem in corde. *Et non minuas,* etc. Mystice. Primitiae frugum, etc., *usque ad* a quo et boni operis initium et perfectio donatur.

VERS. 13.-- *Septies tantum.* Perfectam, scilicet remunerationem. Septenarius enim, etc., *usque ad* sed etiam quatuor principalium virtutum operationem praebet.

VERS. 14.-- *Noli offerre munera,* etc. Apud Deum non est quantitas muneris; nec persona potentis aspicitur: sed dilectio et humilitas cordis. Ideo non debet offerri sacrificium de iniquitate, sed de justo labore.

VERS. 21.-- *Et donec propinquet,* etc. Ad superiora [1218D] respicit, affirmans, quia Dominus orationem humilium misericorditer exaudit, qui non cessant, donec consolationem accipiant.

## CAPUT XXXVI.

VERS. 1.-- *Miserere nostri.* [n: (RAB.)] Ex persona fidelium dirigit orationem ad Deum, ut illos defendat et inimicos deprimat, ut digne correcti Deum iterum agnoscant, et idola deserant.

VERS. 7.-- *Glorifica manum,* etc. [n: (ID.)] Optat, ut divina majestas per manum et dextrum brachium, id est, per Christum, per quem antiqua miracula facta sunt, innovet tempore gratiae, ut veteris legis et novae idem intelligatur esse Deus.

[1219A]VERS. 15.-- *Extolle adversarium,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] Significat per adventum Christi, etc., *usque ad* pro statu Ecclesiae et fidelium salute.

VERS. 16.-- *Sion,* etc. Notitia Scripturae, in qua praedicatur inenarrabilis virtus Dei.

VERS. 17.-- *Et suscita,* etc., Omnes prophetae incarnationi Christi dant testimonium, quod Deus homo factus Ecclesiam sibi desponsaret.

VERS. 19.-- *Secundum benedictionem,* etc. [n: (ID.)] Ordinem scilicet, et ritum sacerdotii, etc., *usque ad* quod Aaron figuravit in temporalibus sacrificiis, hoc impleat in spiritualibus Evangelii.

VERS. 20.-- *Omnem escam.* [n: (ID.)] Postquam praedixit vocationem gentium, etc., *usque ad* sic veracem doctrinam discernamus, et fallacem.

[1219B]VERS. 24.-- *Species mulieris.* Christi gratia, quae per praedicationem animas curat, et carnis concupiscentiam mitigat. Haec in Ecclesia abundat, cujus desiderium est super omnem concupiscentiam hominis, quia in ea decor virtutum et pulchritudo doctrinae. *Super omnem.* Nulla concupiscentia hominis huic desiderio potest comparari: quia, *Fallax gratia et vana est pulchritudo; mulier timens Deum ipsa laudabitur [n: (Prov. XXXI)]*.

VERS. 25.-- *Non est vir.* Christus qui excedit humanam naturam. Unde, *Speciosus forma prae filiis hominum [n: (Psal. XLIV)]*. Hic enim peccatum non fecit, nec est inventus dolus in ore ejus.

VERS. 26.-- *Adjutorium.* Adjutorium Ecclesiae est secundum dispensationem Christi. Unde, *Justum adjutorium [1219C] meum a Domino [n: (Psal. VII)]*, etc. Ipse est infinitatis ejus columna, et laboris requies.

VERS. 28.-- *Qui non habet nidum.* Id est, Ecclesiam, ubi electorum animae filios bonorum operum nutriunt. Unde, *Invenit sibi passer domum, et turtur nidum, ubi reponat pullos suos. [n: (Psal. LXXXIII)]*.



## CAPUT XXXVII.

VERS. 1.-- *Omnis amicus.* [n: (RAB.)] Superius diligentius expressit verum amicum et falsum, dicens: *Et non permanebit in die tribulationis.*

VERS. 2.-- *Sodalis autem.* Verus amicus toto animo diligit, et opere proficit. Unde, *Non diligamus verbo neque lingua, sed opere et veritate [n: (I Joan. III)]*.

VERS. 3.-- *O Praesumptio.* Detestatur hypocrisim, [1219D] cum malus se bonum esse simulat *cooperiendo aridam malitiam,* in qua scilicet non est pinguedo charitatis vel misericordiae.

VERS. 5.-- *Causa ventris.* Pro gula, non pro amicitia. Possunt in falsis amicis haeretici intelligi, qui omnia recte faciunt, quasi animarum consultores, cum sint proditores. Unde, *Attendite a falsis prophetis qui [n: (Matth. VII)]*, etc. *Cum socero.* Socer, qui a parte feminea est cognatus, muliebrem et mutabilem ostendit animum, similiter et zelus qui praecipue est animarum.

VERS. 8.-- *Omnis consiliarius.* Adhuc docet cautelam omnem habendam in suscipiendis amicis et consiliariis. Multi enim se amicos et consiliarios fingunt, [1220A] et insidias tendunt. Unde Jeremias, *Unusquisque se a proximo suo custodiat [n: (Jer. IX)]*.

VERS. 14.-- *Non attendite.* [n: (RAB.)] Diversas species consiliantium enumeravit, in quibus plures personas notavit, quae a veritate discordant. Unde praecepit cum talibus non esse consiliandum, quorum consilium periclitatur. Praevidenda est ergo consiliarii prudentia, fides, voluntas, et religio.

VERS. 18.-- *Anima sancti viri.* Consiliariorum, diversitate ostensa, adjungit, quantum humanae sapientiae sanctorum excellat scientia a Spiritu sancto infusa.

VERS. 22.-- *Vir peritus.* Quia de lingua praedixerat: de bonis malisque doctoribus continuat.

VERS. 28.-- *Vita viri.* [n: (ID.)] Praesens vita hominum [1220B] in incerto non est apud eum. Unde, *Breves dies hominis sunt, numerus mensium apud te est [n: (Job. XIV)]*.

VERS. 32.-- *Noli avidus.* Juxta historiam, parcimoniam laudat, crapulam vituperat, quae ad infirmitatem perducit devorantem. Mystice vero admonet, ut in temporalibus simus temperantes. Unde, *Mel invenisti, comede quod sufficit tibi [n: (Prov. XXV)]*, etc. Et alibi: *Non plus sapere quam oportet [n: (Rom. XII)]*.

## CAPUT XXXVIII.

VERS. 1.-- *Honora medicum.* [n: (RAB.)] Discretos vult nos esse, etc., *usque ad* utrique ergo honorandi, sed spirituales praeferendi.

VERS. 5.-- *Nonne a ligno.* Antiquam tangit historiam [1220C] quia in deserto Sur invenerunt filii Israel aquam amaram, sed Deus ostendit Moysi lignum, quod immissum aquam indulcavit; ubi juxta historiam demonstratur ligni medicina indulcari aquas Mystice autem aqua amara significat legem, cui si confessio crucis et sacramentum jungatur, potabilis efficitur.

VERS. 7.-- *In his curans.* [n: (ID.)] Contra diversas infirmitates, diversa opponunt medici, cibos scilicet et potus, emplastra, et unguenta: ut morbis conveniant medicamenta. Similiter faciunt medici spirituales.

VERS. 10.-- *Averte.* Simile est illud: *Declina a malo, et fac bonum. Et ab omni,* etc., et non tantum corpus, sed ut sis *innocens manibus et mundo corde.*

[1220D]VERS. 11.-- *Da suavitatem.* Panis et vini sacrificium in memoriam Dominicae passionis oblatum, praecipue curat vulnera animarum nec solum vivis, sed et mortuis valde necessarium est.

VERS. 15.-- *Incidet in manus medici.* [n: (ID.)] Aegritudinis et molestiae, etc., *usque ad* et instanter Dominum deprecantur ut dirigat opera eorum, et refrigerium praestet infirmantibus.

VERS. 16.-- *Fili,* etc. Quia de infirmitatibus, et medicorum curationibus disputavit, de mortuorum exsequiis adjungit.

VERS. 21.-- *Memento novissimorum.* [n: (ID.)] Admonitio bonorum patrum ut filii praeparent sibi viaticum bonorum operum.

[1221A]VERS. 22.-- *Neque enim est conversio.* Quasi diceret: Ergo cautus esto in omnibus, ne forte in obitu proximi plus aequo doleas.

VERS. 24.-- *In requie.* Quasi: Morituri memoriam continuo conserva, et confide, et spe conforta, ne in ultimo articulo deficiat.

VERS. 26.-- *Qui tenet aratrum.* Praedicatores sanctos significat, qui omni tempore docendo, exhortando, auditores suos instruunt ut interioris hominis virtutem eliciant, et animam humanam ad imaginem Dei reforment. Unde, *Ut sapiens architectus fundamentum posui [n: (I Cor. III)]*. Et alibi: *Filioli mei quos iterum parturio, donec formetur in vobis Christus [n: (Gal. IV)]*. Quot species virtutum sunt, tot operationes et documenta mentibus electorum doctrina [1221B] imprimunt.

VERS. 28.-- *Sic omnis faber,* etc. Ordo praedicatorum, qui per diversa officia ministerium suum agunt, doctrinam secundum auditores temperant: qui fragiles et infirmos verbis et exemplo formant, ut vasa in honorem faciant.

*Cor suum dabit.* Cum praesentis vitae volubilem conversationem per vestigia bonorum operum subjectis ostendit immutabilem.

VERS. 33.-- *In brachio suo.* [n: (RAB.)] Quia multis exemplis, etc., *usque ad* ut in fornace cordis operationem discipulorum igne solidet charitatis.

## CAPUT XXXIX

VERS. 15.-- *Si permanserit.* [n: (RAB.)] Christi, cujus [1221C] sunt membra, a suo habent omnia: qui est virtus et sapientia Patris.

VERS. 17.-- *Obaudite me.* [n: (ID.)] Intelligite doctrinam meam, mentes electorum per baptismum generatae, et fructum martyrii facite in decursu mortalis vitae.

VERS. 20.-- *Et citharis.* [n: (ID.)] Unde: *Confitemini Domino in cithara [n: (Psal. XXXII)]*. Cithara est ligni ventris in imo concavitas, etc., *usque ad* quae secundum formam psalterii de superius ad nos conveniunt.

VERS. 22.-- *In verbo ejus.* [n: (ID.)] Quando congregavit aquas, etc., *usque ad* vel aqua persecutionis, Dei dispensatione restringitur.

VERS. 24.-- *Opera omnis carnis.* Praesentia Dei antecedit omnia, et quidquid fit temporaliter ei sine [1221D] tempore praesens est. *Nihil ergo novum, neque mutabile est in conspectu ejus [n: (Act. I)]*.

VERS. 26.-- *Non est dicere,* etc. Prohibet nos esse curiosos, et perscrutari quae scire non convenit. Omnia enim in tempore suo manifestabuntur, cum illuminabit Dominus abscondita tenebrarum, et manifestabit consilia cordium.

VERS. 27.-- *Benedictio,* etc. Sicut post diluvii effusionem aquae redibant, ut appareret arida et germinaret; sic post exstinctionem impiorum, datur electis facultas fructificandi.

VERS. 31.-- *Initium necessariae.* Ante diluvium, fructu terrae naturali cibo nutriebantur homines, nedum erant concessae carnes.

[1222A]VERS. 35.-- *Ignis, grando.* [n: (RAB.)] Omnia homini ante peccatum obediebant; post peccatum vero pugnat contra eum orbis terrarum. Inde fames et mors, et mille pericula mortis, bestiae quoque contra eum saeviunt, et rhomphaea coelestis vindictae.

VERS. 37.-- *In mandatis.* Quia juxta supernam sententiam, in tempore opportuno digna ultio peccatores vastabit.

VERS. 38.-- *Propterea ab initio, confirmatus sum.* Ad superiora respicit, ubi ait: *Non est dicere,* etc. Videt enim incomprehensibilia Dei judicia, et investigabiles vias, nec audet inde aliquid temere loqui vel scribere: sed temperate de his disputans, non causam, sed modum divino consilio manifestum dimisit.

VERS. 40.-- *Non est dicere.* Utile dat consilium, [1222B] ut opera ei non incaute discutiamus, sed Creatorem in omnibus laudemus et benedicamus.

VERS. 41.-- *Et nunc in omni tempore suo.* Quasi dicat: Ne dicas priora tempora meliora fuere quam nunc sunt. Virtutes faciunt dies bonos, vitia malos.



## CAPUT XL.

VERS. 2.-- *Cogitationes.* [n: (RAB.)] Enumerat mala quae homo pro peccatis sustinet.

VERS. 6.-- *Modicum.* Quia caro mortua et insensibilis ad tempus requiescere videtur, anima jam sentit dolorem, et post resurrectionem cum corpore suo in poenis vivet aeternis.

VERS. 7.-- *Conturbatus est.* [n: (ID.)] Ideo mali cruciabuntur in poena, etc., *usque ad* nobilium scilicet [1222C] et ignobilium.

VERS. 10.-- *Et propter illos factus est cataclysmus.* Peccanti homini multiplex poena deputata est, ut correctus poeniteat, et deinceps caveat; sed quia negligit, et in poenis proficit, inducit Deus diluvium orbi, ut hominem deleret quem creavit. Ad comparationem vero futurae poenae nihil est quod homo patitur in praesenti.

VERS. 11.-- *Et aquae omnes.* [n: (ID.)] Opera scilicet peccatorum supernae mercedis fructum non acquirunt, sed poenarum interitum.

VERS. 13.-- *Substantiae injustorum.* Inchoant germinare, sed fluctuant in tentatione, et subito arescunt ad primum persecutionis aestum.

VERS. 15.-- *Nepotes impiorum non multi.* Saepe [1222D] videmus progeniem impiorum cito deficere, maxime cum filii imitantur iniquitatem patrum.

VERS. 18.-- *Vita sibi sufficientis.* Dulcis est somnus operanti, sive parum, sive multum comedat. *Invenies thesaurum.* Vere enim Christianum se esse probat, qui Christi mandata credit et facit.

VERS. 20.-- *Vinum et musica laetificant cor.* Haec naturaliter mulcent et exhilarant animam, sed dilectio sapientiae et lingua suaviter docens multo plus confortat intellectum.

VERS. 22.-- *Gratiam et speciem desiderabit oculus.* Ornatum scilicet templi et culturae diversitatem, quae prior populus sub lege habuit, praedicatio Evangelii in orbe seminata, bonorum operum virore excellit

[1223A]VERS. 26.-- *Facultates et virtutes.* [n: (RAB.)] Divitiae datae in Domino, etc., *usque ad* et haec et omnes facultates mundi.

VERS. 30.-- *Vir respiciens.* Stultum est enim otiari, et de alieno labore mercedem quaerere. Percipiet enim unusquisque secundum opera sua.

VERS. 32.-- *In ore imprudentis conculcabitur inopia,* etc. Cui placet otiose torpere, nec proximis docendo prodesse, tandem doloribus inferni et sera poenitentia aestuabit.

## CAPUT XLI.

VERS. 1.-- *O mors,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] Qui prosperitatem mundi et divitias amat, amara est illi mors corporalis, quia futurae vitae gaudia negligit.

[1223B]VERS. 5.-- *Hoc judicium.* [n: (ID.)] Commune est omni carni, nec quisquam evadere potest, etiamsi centum aut mille annos vixerit aut ultra; unde: *Quis est homo qui vivet, et non videbit mortem? [n: (Psal. LXXXVIII)]*.

VERS. 8.-- *Filii abominationum.* Abominabiles sunt filii peccatorum, qui scilicet, impios patres imitati sunt.

VERS. 10.-- *De patre impio.* Qui male filios nutrit, vel exemplo perdit, reus est eorum perditionis. Vel, qui mala opera de prava voluntate gignit, damnabitur pro eis

VERS. 13.-- *In perditionem.* Superioribus respondet, in quibus de morte temporali disputavit: quia sicut homo de terra creatus pro peccato originali in [1223C] terram redit, quamvis in incorruptione surrecturus; sic impii pro peccatis suis maledicti, in aeternam perditionem cum corpore et anima ibunt.

VERS. 15.-- *Curam habe de bono nomine,* etc. Ut bene et religiose vivas. Sic autem acquiritur bonum nomen.

VERS. 18.-- *Melior est homo qui abscondit stultitiam suam,* etc. Qui abscondet frumentum, maledicetur in populis, benedictio autem super caput vendentium.

VERS. 19.-- *Verumtamen revertimini in his quae procedunt.* Quia bonum nomen et bonam et vitam utilem esse praedixit, et occultantes scientiam reprehendit, suadet ut revertantur ad studium docendi, quia non est bonum irreverentem et inobedientem [1223D] esse suo doctori.

VERS. 20.-- *Non est bonum omnem irreverentiam observare.* Juxta litteram, nos instruit ut a vitiis caveamus, et virtutibus operam demus, et ne spretis melioribus, eligamus pejora, quae sequitur confusio sempiterna.

VERS. 26.-- *Non avertas faciem tuam a proximo tuo,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] Cum angeli colligent de Ecclesia omnia scandala, etc., *usque ad* et fornicationibus haereticorum se miscuit.

VERS. 27.-- *Ne respicias mulierem alieni viri,* etc. Cupiditatem carnalem quae debet subesse spiritui, hanc non debemus scrutari et suggestionibus ejus subjici.

## CAPUT XLII.

[1224A]

VERS. 1.-- *Non duplices sermonem,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] Prohibet de occulto cordis bonum et malum simul dicere; unde: Nunquid fons de eodem foramine emanat dulcem et amaram aquam?

VERS. 4.-- *De aequalitate staterae,* etc. [n: (ID.)] Ubique sequenda est aequitas, etc., *usque ad* subjectos quoque cum discretione disciplinae regamus.

*De aequalitate staterae.* Quantum hypocrisis et dolus Domino displiceat ostenditur his verbis: *Statera dolosa abominatio est apud Deum.* Qui aliter causam pauperis quam potentis librat; vel sua errata leviora quam aliorum putat; vel qui imponunt in humeros hominum onera importabilia; vel qui bona in publico, mala in occulto agit, abominabilis est [1224B] Domino.

VERS. 5.-- *Et servo pessimo.* Significat servum qui verbis non corrigitur, verberibus esse coercendum. Servus quoque vitiorum severa disciplina corrigendus est.

VERS. 7.-- *Ubi manus multae,* etc. Admonet ubi diversae sunt voluntates spirituali lucro inhiantes, caute esse dispensandum. Alii enim tentandi, alii discendi voto quaerunt verbum, sed non omnia omnibus conveniunt.

VERS. 8.-- *De disciplina.* Qui congrua disciplina unumquemque arguit, eruditum se et probabilem doctorem in conspectu sanctorum ostendit. Nec aetas juvenilis in doctore despicienda, quem vita et discretio commendat.

[1224C]VERS. 9.-- *Filia patris.* [n: (RAB.)] Mystice filia patris, etc., *usque ad* vel transgrediatur legem Dei facta sterilis in omnibus bonis.

*Filia patris.* Docet, ad litteram, parentes sobolis suae curam gerere, et cum disciplina nutrire, et ne lasciviae et voluptati frena relaxent.

VERS. 11.-- *Super filiam luxuriosam,* etc. Quae diligentem quaerit custodiam. Si enim dimittitur suae voluntati, doctorem confundit et in multitudine populi erubescere facit. Unde, periculose tibi ministrat, cujus vultum frequenter attendis. Nam impudici oculi non norunt animae pulchritudinem considerare, sed corporum.

VERS. 14.-- *Melior est enim iniquitas viri,* etc. [n: (ID.)] Mulier aut sexum significat, etc., *usque ad* [1224D] quia res confusione dignas gerit.

VERS. 15.-- *Memor ero igitur operum,* etc. [n: (ID.)] Hucusque de diversis rebus disputavit, etc., *usque ad* et postea patrum fortia facta describit.

VERS. 19.-- *Cognovit enim Dominus,* etc. Quia omnes aetates mundi praesentes sunt ei, apud quem nihil praeteritum, nihil futurum est; ipse solus revelat mysteria, qui scit singulorum corda, qui omnes cogitatus et sermones inspicit.

VERS. 21.-- *Magnalia sapientiae.* Quando prophetis scilicet et apostolis sacramentum consilii sui absconditum a saeculis et generationibus fidelibus revelavit. Ipse enim est ante omnes, et post omnes, cui nihil additur, nihil minuitur.

[1225A]VERS. 23.-- *Et tanquam scintilla.* Tanquam scintillam in opera Dei consideramus, quia vix parvam notitiam inde percipimus.

VERS. 25.-- *Omnia duplicia,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] Ita ordinavit Deus omnia, ut quae sibi videntur esse contraria conveniant, ut elementa vel quatuor tempora.



## CAPUT XLIII.

VERS. 1.-- *Altitudinis,* etc. [n: (ID.)] pulchritudo firmamenti, etc., *usque ad* nullus corporeis oculis divinitatis splendorem potest sufferre.

VERS. 3.-- *Fornacem custodiens.* Quia superbos, pro cogitatione, locutione, et operatione mala, excruciat aeterna flamma.

VERS. 5.-- *Et in sermonibus ejus,* etc. [n: (ID.)] [1225B] Mysticis verbis superborum ludit intellectum. *Festinavit,* etc. Cum in praedicatione Evangelii praeparata est via salutis et aditus regni coelestis.

VERS. 6.-- *Et luna,* etc. [n: (ID.)] Postquam de sole disputavit, etc., *usque ad* sed rectius aprili deputatur, quia in ipso vel incipit, vel desinit, vel totus includitur.

VERS. 7.-- *Luminare quod minuitur,* etc. Luna non habet nativum splendorem, sed a sole accipit: sic et Ecclesia a Christo, quae in persecutione videtur minui, sed in parte clarescit; crescit enim mirabiliter in consummatione.

VERS. 9.-- *Vas castrorum,* etc. Quia in ipsa consistit multitudo fidelium, quae in firmamento veritatis et divinae praedicationis per totum orbem gloriose [1225C] resplendet.

VERS. 10.-- *Species coeli,* etc. Ornatus Ecclesiae, sanctorum plenitudo, quos Deus excelsus ordinavit, ut praedicatione Evangelii illustrarent. Hi *in verbis sanctis* et in doctrina verae fidei permanentes, exspectant judicium Dei.

VERS. 11.-- *In verbis.* Quia in patientia sua possident animas, praecincti lumbos; et lucernas tenentes in manibus suis, exspectant Dominum suum, quando revertatur a nuptiis.

VERS. 12.-- *Vide arcum,* etc. Scriptum Veteris vel Novi Testamenti. Hic fidelibus suave jugum ostenditur, contumacibus arma terribilia.

VERS. 13.-- *Gyravit coelum,* etc. Quando per virtutem et sapientiam Dei, id est, Christum, Vetus et [1225D] Novum Testamentum conditum est.

VERS. 16.-- *Et confracti sunt lapides grandinis.* Doctores, qui terram humani cordis irrigant, et tempestatem increpationis in se gerunt, et in tempore effundunt, et confringunt lapides grandinis; increpando, scilicet duritiam pravi cordis lapident vitale gramen.

VERS. 17.-- *Aspirabit Notus.* [n: (RAB.)] Qui et Auster, etc., *usque ad* potentes ad Christiani nominis persecutionem, et aliquando ad poenitentiam.

VERS. 18.-- *Tempestas.* Varia tentamenta per malignos spiritus Deus irrogat, ut fervorem fidei et dilectionem frigescere faciant.

VERS. 21.-- *Gelu sicut salem,* etc. Id est, sterilitatem; [1226A] ubi enim sal spargitur, sterilitas sequitur: diabolus vero per frigus infidelitatis terrena corda ad bona opera sterilia facit.

VERS. 24.-- *Medicina,* etc. Omnis eloquentia deficit in comparatione ejus, nec sufficit virtutem ejus enarrare.

VERS. 26.-- *Qui navigant mare,* etc. Multa sunt ad litteram pericula maris, et ibi mirabilia Dei opera in variis bestiis, sicut naturalium rerum scriptores tradiderunt. In mari quoque hujus mundi sunt multa monstra daemoniorum et multae eorum insidiae.

VERS. 34.-- *Ne laboretis,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] Comprehendere quod est incomprehensibile. Unde non quaeras opes ad quas pertingere non possis.

## CAPUT XLIV.

[1226B]

VERS. 1.-- *Laudemus viros,* etc. Moraliter disputando, allegoriamque et anagogem in plerisque tangendo, mysteria divini sacramenti edidit; nunc de sanctis patribus narrare incipit. *Parentes nostros.* Patriarchas, qui divina locutione et visione fruebantur; et Prophetas, qui, Spiritu sancto repleti, multa Christi et Ecclesiae mysteria praecinuerunt.

VERS. 12.-- *In Testamentis stetit,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] Haec juxta historiam de patriarchis, etc., *usque ad* quando semen bonorum operum coelesti mercede compensabitur.

VERS. 16.-- *Henoch placuit Deo.* Non ab Adam, etc., *usque ad* ut det hominibus consilium poenitendi.

VERS. 17.-- *Noe inventus est,* etc. Quando pereunte [1226C] mundo diluvio reservatus est, ut poenitentiam gentibus praedicaret, et exemplo demonstraret quod qui Deo devote serviunt, ab aeterno interitu liberantur. Cum eo Deus pactum statuit, ne ultra perderet aquis diluvii omnem carnem [n: (Gen. XVII)]. Significat autem rectores, qui inter fluctus saeculi arcam, id est Ecclesiam, regunt, et praedicant baptismum poenitentiae, orationibus et sacrificiis Deum placantes humano generi.

VERS. 21.-- *In carne ejus facit stare testamentum,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] Ut significaretur renovata natura nostra per baptismum Christi, post exspoliationem veteris hominis.

VERS. 22.-- *Ideo jurejurando,* etc. Duplex est promissio Abrahae. In arena maris exprimuntur steriles [1226D] Judaei; in similitudine stellarum, fideles Christiani, qui resurrectionis lumine coruscabunt sicut astra coeli.

VERS. 26.-- *Et dedit illi haereditatem,* etc. Gentilis populi, qui posterior ad gratiam fidei et baptismi regenerationem accessit, cui plenitudo paternae benedictionis provenit.

## CAPUT XLV.

VERS. 6.-- *Praecepta.* In monte Sinai, scilicet legem dedit ei et praecepta vitae, cum eo loquens in nube.

VERS. 9.-- *Et circumcinxit eum,* etc. Describit ritum veteris sacerdotii et ornatum pontificis, quae omnia figura erant Novi Testamenti, et veri sacerdotis Jesu Christi. *Et induit.* Vestimenta pontificis sunt opera virtutum: sapientia, doctrina.

VERS. 14.-- *Corona aurea,* etc. In qua erat nomen omnipotentis Dei, quae significat honorificentiam divinae majestatis, quoniam super omnia statuere debemus, ut in omnibus actibus nostris et sermonibus honorificetur Deus *per Jesum Christum, qui est caput nostrum [n: (I Petr. IV)]*.

VERS. 17.-- *Sacrificia.* [n: (RAB.)] Quomodo Moyses Aaron, etc., *usque ad* Christi enim sacerdotium et ritus sacrificiorum in aeternum manebit.

VERS. 28.-- *Phinees filius Eleazari.* [n: (ID.)] Phinees, sicut scriptum est in libro Numerorum [n: (Cap. XXV)], etc., *usque ad* ad montem fortitudinis, id est Christum, [1227B] feliciter pervenit.

VERS. 31.-- *Et testamentum David.* [n: (ID.)] Significat quod David in distributione ministeriorum Dei, etc., *usque ad* et in tabernaculo ministrorum vices ordinavit.

## CAPUT XLVI.

VERS. 1.-- *Fortis in bello Jesus Nave.* [n: (RAB.)] Jesus et opere et sermone Christum significat, etc., *usque ad* triumphans principatus et potestates in semetipso.

VERS. 4.-- *Quis ante illum,* etc. (ID). Quomodo in occursu Josue impeditus est sol, etc., *usque ad* breviabuntur in tempore perditionis.

VERS. 9.-- *A peccatis.* Desperationis, quando exploratorum rumoribus auditis desperaverunt intrare [1227C] terram.

VERS. 13.-- *Et judices singuli,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] Post Josue, successerunt judices qui populum Dei ab hostibus defendebant; et post Christi passionem, apostoli rectores Ecclesiae Dei.

VERS. 14.-- *Ut sit memoria illorum,* etc. Quia in recta fide perseveraverunt, ut memoria eorum perpetua benedictione firmaretur. *Ossa.* Robur bonorum operum mercede donatur, ut memoria nominis eorum ad posteros cum gloria transferatur.

VERS. 16.-- *Dilectus a Domino,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] Narrat historia quod Dominus Samueli infanti, etc., *usque ad* pronuntiat malis rectoribus poenam futuram et mortem perpetuam.

## CAPUT XLVII.

[1227D]

VERS. 1.-- *Post haec surrexit Nathan.* Ad litteram, facta David commemorat, de quibus liber Regum et Paralipomenon plenissime narrant.

VERS. 2.-- *Quasi adeps.* Significat eum gratia Spiritus sancti repletum, a carnalium consortio vita et moribus separatum.

VERS. 3.-- *Cum leonibus lusit.* [n: (RAB.)] David significat Christum, etc., *usque ad* et dedit illi nomen, quod est super omne nomen.

VERS. 14.-- *Post ipsum surrexit filius sensatus.* [n: (ID.)] Mystice, Salomon, etc., *usque ad* sicut in una area bonos significant grana, malos vero palea.

VERS. 23.-- *Ut faceres imperium,* etc. [n: (ID.)] Quia [1228A] decem tribus secutae sunt Jeroboam, et duae Roboam; de Ephraim fuit Jeroboam, qui primus in decem tribubus crudeliter regnavit.

VERS. 27.-- *Et dereliquit post se,* etc. [n: (ID.)] Mystice, Roboam, qui interpretatur *latitudo populi,* etc., *usque ad* in regula catholicae fidei permansit.

VERS. 28.-- *Avertit gentem consilio suo.* Credens scilicet consilio juvenum.



## CAPUT XLVIII.

VERS. 1.-- *Et surrexit Elias.* [n: (RAB.)] Qui duos quinquagenarios ab Ozia rege missos coelesti igne combussit [n: (IV Reg. I)].

VERS. 2.-- *Qui induxit.* [n: (ID.)] Mystice, fames trium annorum verbi Dei et fidei Trinitatis inediam figuravit, etc., *usque ad* ut postea veniret qui nec [1228B] translatus nec subvectus, coelum aethereum sua virtute penetraret.

VERS. 13.-- *Elias quidem in turbine,* etc. [n: (ID.)] Cum non sit discipulus super magistrum, etc., *usque ad* qui enim firma fide tangit mortem Christi, particeps est ejus resurrectionis.

*In Eliseo completus.* Qui oravit die: *Fiat spiritus tuus duplex in me,* et obtinuit. Unde in patientia et virtute insuperabilis fuit, qui in vita et in morte multa signa fecit.

VERS. 17.-- *Relicta est gens perpauca.* Quia domus David, et tribus Juda, et Benjamin, non penitus abjecerunt culturam Dei, sed alii eorum fuerunt idolatrae, sicut Joram et Achaz: alii adhaeserunt Deo, sicut Ezechias et Josias.

[1228C]VERS. 19.-- *Ezechias munivit civitatem suam,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] Quod Ezechias fontem obturat, etc., *usque ad* civitatem exstinctis hostibus liberatam in Paralipomenon plene ostenditur.

## CAPUT XLIX.

VERS. 1. *Memoria Josiae.* [n: (RAB.)] Memoria Josiae regis, etc., *usque ad* ipse zelo Dei mundat terram Judae et Jerusalem ab omnibus abominationibus, qui ait: *Zelus domus tuae comedit me.*

VERS. 5.-- *Praeter David, et Ezechiam, et Josiam,* etc. Hi tres comparatione aliorum non dicuntur peccasse. Quod enim peccaverunt, condigna poenitentia deleverunt, et devotione et pietate Deo placuerunt.

[1228D]VERS. 8.-- *Incenderunt electa civitatem sanctitatis,* etc. [n: (ID.)] Quidam hunc locum in persona Christi intelligunt, etc., *usque ad* his autem destructis, aedificavit Ecclesiam Dei.

VERS. 10.-- *Ezechiel qui vidit,* etc. [n: (ID.)] Mystice, Ezechiel, etc., *usque ad* et poenitentibus praedixisse remedia.

VERS. 11.-- *In imbre.* Significat quod praedicaverit super peccatores venturam esse pluviam vindictae, et per viam mandatorum Dei gradientibus promiserit consolationem misericordiae.

VERS. 13.-- *Nam et ipse,* etc. Quia Christum signat, qui est imago Dei: ut quicunque crediderit in Deum, hic quasi annulo signetur.

[1229A]VERS. 14.-- *Et Jesum filium Josedec.* Quia per gratiam Jesu Christi, qui est rex noster et sacerdos, post captivitatem diabolicae oppressionis, reaedificatur Ecclesia.

VERS. 15.-- *Nehemias.* [n: (RAB.)] *Consolator Deus,* vel *consolatus a Domino,* etc., *usque ad* qui aedificat civitatem Dei, id est Ecclesiam, et consolatur moerentes.

VERS. 16.-- *Nemo,* etc. Enoch, *dedicatio.* Hic Christum significat, qui aedificavit et consecravit Ecclesiam sanguine suo; qui sine peccato venit in mundum, et cum gloria suscepturus est in coelum.

VERS. 17.-- *Ut Joseph.* Joseph, sicut Jacob pater ejus, terram promissionis desiderabat, Aegyptum detestabatur; instruens nos ut desideremus terram [1229B] viventium, ut quiescamus in pace.

VERS. 18.-- *Et ossa ipsius visitata sunt.* [n: (RAB.)] Significat quod Joseph, etc., *usque ad* et sepelierunt in Sichem, quae est Neapolis, urbs Samaritanorum.

VERS. 19.-- *Seth et Sem,* etc. Seth filius Adam, et Sem primogenitus Noe, tam fide quam moribus hominibus sui temporis praelati sunt; in quibus Christus significatur, qui Deus et homo est.

## CAPUT L.

VERS. 1.-- *Simon Oniae filius.* [n: (RAB.)] Ad homines in tempore suo pervenit, etc., *usque ad* cum vitam Simonis et mores tam expresse describat Jesus.

VERS. 3.-- *Putei aquarum.* Profunditates Scripturarum, quae in divinis libris sub figuris latent, [1229C] sed ore praedicatorum redundant, quasi mare ad saturitatem plurimorum.

VERS. 5.-- *Et ingressum domus atrii amplificavit.* Quia in rudibus, quos signat atrium; et in perfectis, qui signantur per domum, magistrorum excrescit meritum.

VERS. 11.-- *In accipiendo ipsum stolam,* etc. Ordo praedicatorum accipiendo stolam gloriae, et vestiendo se consummatione virtutum, judicium dignitatis suae, et ornatum fidei, et vestitum bonae operationis demonstrat. Haec enim debent in sacerdotibus apparere, ut digne possint docere.

VERS. 13.-- *In accipiendo autem partes de manu sacerdotis.* Partes accipit de manu sacerdotis, qui bonae operationis actum exigit a ministris.

VERS. 15.-- *Et consummatione fungens in ara.* Consummata oblatio datur excelso Regi, quando corpus Christi offertur Deo.

VERS. 17.-- *Effudit in fundamento.* In commemorationem Christi, qui est fundamentum Ecclesiae, hujus oblationis est odor suavissimus Deo omnipotenti.

VERS. 18.-- *Tunc exclamaverunt filii Aaron.* Christi sacerdotes praedicationem exhibuerunt per passionem consummatam. Ductiles tubae bene dicuntur, quia praedicatores tanto crescunt quanto tribulationum malleis percutiuntur.

VERS. 19.-- *Tunc omnis populus,* etc. Cum officium ecclesiasticum per ministros altaris agitur in [1230A] memoriam Christi, populus, ad laudem Dei provocatus, prosternit se in faciem, id est, cordis sui exhibet humilitatem. *Dare preces Omnipotenti.* Quia quidquid amore Dei agitur, coram Deo est oratio et odor suavitatis; quia omnis Ecclesia satagit ut perseveret in prece usque ad finem mundi, quando corpus Christi in incorruptione honorabitur, et membra capiti suo conjungentur.

VERS. 21.-- *Et rogavit populus,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] Quia quidquid in unitate fidei Deo offertur, apud eum recipitur; quidquid extra, impietati deputatur. Magnus fit in Ecclesia sonus, quando orantibus sacerdotibus et benedicentibus respondet omnis populus: Amen: qui sonus tam ad clamorem vocis quam ad devotionem cordis pertinet.

[1230B]VERS. 22.-- *Tunc descendens,* etc. Coetus sanctorum exsultans. *Extulit.* Quando gratias agit pro perfectione laboris in salute universi populi, tunc laudes multiplicat, orationem iterat, quia nunquam a laudibus cessat.

VERS. 23.-- *Ostendere virtutem Dei.* Praedicare scilicet misericordiam ejus, qui dat nobis jucunditatem cordis, et pacem in temporibus aeternis, ut omnes viri Israelitae, et amatores Regis aeterni, praedicent potentiam et bonitatem Dei in liberatione populi sui.

VERS. 27.-- *Duas gentes,* etc. Ruina duplex, gentilitas scilicet, quae idololatria polluta est et conversatione vana.

VERS. 29.-- *Doctrinam sapientiae,* etc. Opus suum [1230C] commendat, ostendens quam utile sit legenti, meditanti et operanti.

## CAPUT LI.

VERS. 1.-- *Oratio Jesu filii Sirach.* Melius ad totam Ecclesiam refertur, quam ad unam personam, quia in ea multae species tribulationum et diversa solatia describuntur.

*Confitebor tibi, Domine rex.* [n: (RAB.)] Jesus Christus adjutor et protector est sponsae suae, qui tradidit semetipsum pro ea, ut liberaret eam a perditione originalis peccati.

VERS. 5.-- *Portis tribulationum.* Haec sunt ora principum et tyrannorum, unde minae prodeunt et fraudulentiae, quae servos Dei negare fidem compellunt.

[1230D]VERS. 6.-- *A pressura flammae.* Hoc tribus pueris contigit in camino ignis corporaliter; sed omnes sancti ab aestu persecutionis liberantur spiritualiter.

VERS. 9.-- *Et vita mea appropinquans erat inferno.* Quia vita carnis quotidie deficiendo ad mortem tendit. Mortem enim *infernum* vocat, quia mors carnis, primi peccati vindicta est, sicut infernus peccantium animarum poena perpetua.

VERS. 10.-- *Circumdederunt me undique,* etc. Videns Ecclesia se ab hostibus circumdari, et humanum deesse solatium, a Deo quaerit adjutorium, a quo est omne bonum, cui attribuit quod liberatur ab inimicis.

[1231A]VERS. 18.-- *Cum adhuc junior essem.* [n: (RAB.)] In juventute, vel pueritia, etc., *usque ad* quomodo ab infantia quaesierit sapientiam.

*Priusquam oberrarem,* etc. Signat se ante errorem pueritiae vel juventutis desiderasse sapientiam, et a Domino postulasse, et usque ad novissimum perseverasse.

VERS. 19.-- *Tanquam praecox uva.* Decorem sapientiae comparat praecoquae uvae, ut ostendat jucunditatem apud eam esse. Praecoqua enim uva dicitur eo quod cito maturescat.

VERS. 24.-- *Consiliatus sum,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] Prius dicit se consilium inisse ut faceret illam, etc., *usque [1232A] ad* sic enim confirmatus, perveniet ad fructum sapientiae.

VERS. 29.-- *Venter meus.* Commotus ad poenitentiam per sapientiae notitiam. *Propterea.* Ad perfectionem sapientiae pervenire non est humani studii, sed divini muneris.

VERS. 30.-- *Dedit mihi Dominus,* etc. Bona merces est lingua erudita, quae fecit fratres instruere et corrigere.

VERS. 37.-- *Laetetur anima.* Magna est jucunditas cordis, si recordatur misericordiam superni judicis.

## CHAPTER ONE.

[1183C]

VERS. 1.-- *All wisdom,* etc. [n: (RAB. in Eccli., tom. III.)] He begins from the eternal wisdom of God, which is Christ, who is always with the Father before the ages, according to that word: *In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God [n: (Joan. I)]*. *Is from the Lord God.* Because Christ, the fountain of life, the true light, is born of the Father, *and all things were made by him, and without him was made nothing [n: (Ibid.)]*. Whoever lacks this wisdom walks in darkness, and knows not where he goes. *For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God; and the prudence of the flesh is death [n: (Sap. XI)]*.

VERS. 2.-- *The sand of the sea, and the drops of rain.* [n: (RAB. ubi supra )]. He compares bodily things with spiritual, so that from the most difficult a thing altogether impossible may be estimated. [1183D] For if these things, which were established in a fixed number and measure and weight, no one can count, how much less shall he be able to search out the wisdom of God, which is without beginning and without end, unutterable, inestimable?

VERS. 4.-- *She was created before all things.* Created according to his humanity in the counsel of God the Father, that is, he was predestined to be incarnate for the salvation of the human race. And it is to be noted that, on account of the unity of the person, Christ is sometimes said to be begotten, sometimes created.

VERS. 5.-- *The fountain of wisdom.* The origin of all wisdom proceeds from the Word of God, which, God from God, abides always with the Father in the heavens; but having entered the world through the dispensation of his humanity, it gave the commandments of salvation, whence: *Thou hast the words of eternal life [n: (Joan. VI)]*.

VERS. 6.-- *The root of wisdom.* He shows that no one is able [1184C] to penetrate the depth of God, or the [sic: *magnituditudinem*] of his goodness and mercy. Wherefore, for the liberation and enlightenment of the human race, he deigned to become man; whence: *Who shall declare his generation [n: (Isa. LIII)]* ?

VERS. 9.-- *He himself created her.* That is, he dispensed the coming of the Only-begotten through the Word coeternal with himself together with the Holy Spirit: how through the Virgin's childbearing he should come for the salvation of the world, and should repair his creatures, and should call man back to the knowledge and love of himself, giving him the gift of the Holy Spirit, that by his gift he should be loosed for ever.

VERS. 11.-- *The fear of the Lord is glory,* etc. *Blessed is the man that feareth the Lord: he desireth exceedingly in his commandments. Glory and riches are in his house [n: (Psal. III)]*, etc. [var: Vulg. *volet nimis*, "he shall delight exceedingly," for *cupit nimis*] *The fear [1184D] of the Lord.* There are two kinds of fear. Of the one it is said, *Fear* [is not in charity] *of the soul in charity, [n: (Joan. IV)]*, etc. They who have this fear cease from sinning for dread of hell, and amend their life: this fear brings charity in, but it is also cast out. For he who fears in this way does not yet love nor desire good things, but guards against evil ones; yet nevertheless he corrects himself, and begins to desire good things. Of the other it is written, *The fear of the Lord is holy, it endureth for ever and ever [n: (Psal. XVIII)]*. [var: Vulg. *permanens*, "enduring"] For every man fears lest he lose the good things, and the presence of God, which he desires to enjoy for ever; of which it is said:

VERS. 12.-- *The fear of the Lord shall delight the heart.* This bestows inward sweetness, and in the time to come eternal life.

VERS. 14.-- *Love,* [n: (RAB.)] The true love of God [1185A] is wisdom, etc., *as far as* it shall itself be the reward in the time to come; whence: *Thou shalt fill me with joy with thy countenance, delights at thy right hand [n: (Psal. XV)]*, etc.

VERS. 17.-- *The fear of the Lord.* Without the fear of God, and the keeping of his commandments, there is no religion; whence: *If any man think himself to be religious, not bridling his tongue, but deceiving his own heart, this man's religion is vain [n: (Jac. I)]*.

VERS. 19.-- *To him that feareth the Lord.* That is, to him who by the fear of God keeps the rule of justice in faith and in teaching and in work.

VERS. 23.-- *And he saw.* [n: (RAB.)] All things are in his sight; for each one he keeps a worthy recompense.

VERS. 25.-- *The branches.* Through wisdom man has [1185B] the divine knowledge of avoiding evil, and the understanding of doing good; for it works both in the hearer unto the end; whence: *He that hearkeneth to me shall not be confounded, and they that work by me shall not sin. They that explain me shall have life everlasting [n: (Eccli. XXIV)]*. *The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord. A good understanding to all that do it [n: (Psal. CX)]*.

VERS. 26.-- *In the treasures.* In the meditation of the law both are declared: namely, how evils are to be avoided, and how spiritual wisdom is to be learned and good works to be practised, in which things is true religion. *The understanding of wisdom.* Which forbids sins and carnal desires; whence: *A pestilent man loveth not him that correcteth himself, nor doth he go to the wise [n: (Prov. XV)]*. [var: Vulg. *corripit*, "him that rebuketh him"]

VERS. 27.-- *Fear,* etc. Because through penance [1185C] it cleanses from past sins, or forbids those that are to be committed. For he who does not correct himself through the fear of God falls into the abyss of sin.

VERS. 30.-- *Good sense.* Whence in the Proverbs, *The lips of the wise preserve them [n: (Prov. XIV)]*. And elsewhere: *The crafty man doeth all things with counsel: but he that is a fool hath laid open his folly [n: (Ibid. XXXI)]*. [var: Vulg. *aperiet*, "shall lay open"] It belongs, therefore, to a wise man to hold his words, and to carry out all things with moderation. *They shall declare his sense.* With an even mind, rendering not evil for evil, but good for good.

VERS. 33.-- *Son, coveting wisdom.* How thou mayest come to wisdom, wisdom herself shows, because without the keeping of justice no one comes to the summit of wisdom; whence James: *Who is a wise man,* saith he, *and endued with knowledge among you? let him show [1185D] good conversation in the meekness of wisdom [n: (Jac. III)]*. [var: Vulg. *ostendat ex bona conversatione operationem suam*, "let him show, by a good conversation, his work"]

VERS. 34.-- *For wisdom and discipline.* (RAB). As has often been said, *The fear of the Lord is the keeping of wisdom and discipline [n: (Prov. XIII)]*, to which belong right faith and temperance of manners, because without faith it is impossible to please God, and the life of good men is always tranquil; whence in Matthew: *Learn of me, because I am meek and humble of heart, and you shall find rest for your souls [n: (Matth. XI)]*. For he who truly fears God cannot be without faith and good works, which fill a man with virtues and make him acceptable to God. Whence: *To the man that is good in his sight God hath given wisdom and knowledge and joy. But to the sinner [1186A] he hath given affliction and superfluous care [n: (Eccle. II)]*.

VERS. 36.-- *With a double heart.* A man double of mind is inconstant in all his ways: he, namely, who wishes to rejoice with the world and to reign with Christ.

VERS. 37.-- *A hypocrite..* Bearing one thing in his heart, and showing another in his work. Whence: *Beware of false prophets, who come to you in the clothing of sheep [n: (Matth. VII)]*.

VERS. 38.-- *Attend unto them,* etc. It is manifest that he who follows heretics purchases damnation for his own soul, because in the judgment the hidden things of hearts shall be revealed, and it shall be rendered to every man according to his works; *for God will destroy all that speak a lie [n: (Psal. LXI)]*. Who abhorreth the bloody [1186B] and deceitful man; whence: Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy. And elsewhere: *The lord of that servant shall come, and shall divide him, and shall appoint his portion with the hypocrites: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth [n: (Matth. XXIV)]*.



## CHAPTER II.

VERS. 1.-- *Son, coming,* etc. He has shown what is to be avoided; now he shows what is to be done, saying: *Son, when thou comest to the service of God, stand in justice and in fear.* For he who wishes to withdraw himself from the enticements of the world and to live godly in Christ suffers persecution. For while he makes ready to be girded for the divine service, he stirs up the war of the devil against himself; and while he subdues some vices, he struggles against others, and by the divine dispensation it is so ordered that he both overcomes and is overcome, lest he be lifted up. But [1186C] because humility and patience are necessary to him, there follows, *Humble thy heart, and endure,* etc.

VERS. 4.-- *Have patience.* As if to say: *In your patience you shall possess your souls [n: (Luc. XXI)]*, because, namely, patience is the root and the keeper of all the virtues. And it is to be known that patience is exercised in three ways. For by God we are scourged, but care must be taken that we do not murmur; from our neighbour we bear persecutions and losses and insults, and care must be taken that we do not render evil for evil; by the adversary we are tempted, but we must look ahead lest we be bent to the delight of sin or to consent to it, or seek present things in return for these, but rather await things to come.

VERS. 6.-- *Believe God, and he will recover thee.* [n: (RAB.)] [1186D] The afflicted man must believe, and direct the steps of his works in the sight of God, and hope in him; whence: *Reveal thy way to the Lord, and hope in him, and he will do it. [n: (Psal. XXXVI)]*. Hence Jeremiah says: *Blessed is he that trusteth in the Lord, and God shall be his confidence [n: (Jer. XVII)]*, etc. [var: Vulg. *Benedictus vir qui confidit in Domino, et erit Dominus fiducia ejus*]

VERS. 7.-- *Ye that fear the Lord,* etc. *The Lord is well pleased with them that fear him, and in them that hope upon his mercy [n: (Psal. CXLVI)]*. For he who truly fears patiently awaits his mercy: *But they that forsake God shall be confounded, and shall be written in the earth [n: (Jer. XVII)]*. [var: Vulg. *omnes qui te derelinquunt confundentur; recedentes a te in terra scribentur*]

VERS. 8.-- *Ye that fear the Lord, believe him.* He exhorts them that fear the Lord to believe him, that they may come to a certain reward; whence: *For the just man liveth [1187A] by faith [n: (Rom. I)]*; whence: *Be of good heart, son, thy sins are forgiven thee [n: (Matth. IX)]*. And elsewhere: *Thy faith hath made thee whole [n: (Ibid., X)]*.

VERS. 9.-- *Ye that fear the Lord, hope in him.* He commends three things to them that fear God: to believe, to hope, to love; because by faith, hope and charity God is truly worshipped, and one comes to contemplation, which is eternal blessedness.

VERS. 11.-- *Look ye,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] Here too he says three things, etc., *as far as* because *a sacrifice to God is an afflicted spirit [n: (Psal. L)]*, etc. And, *God is nigh unto all that call upon him in truth [n: (Psal. CXLIV)]*. [var: Vulg. *Prope est Dominus omnibus invocantibus eum … in veritate*]

VERS. 14.-- *Woe to them that are of a double heart,* etc. He warned that no one should come to God with a double heart; but now he says, *Woe to them that are of a double heart and of wicked lips.* For he who [1187B] thinks and speaks crooked things, and persists in crooked works, unless he repent, shall perish for ever. *Going into the land by two ways* is he who does evil and hopes for good; or, he who follows the works of the flesh and judges that he is bringing to perfection the sanctification of the spirit in fear; or, he who displays in work what is God's, and seeks in thought what is the world's. Such men indeed are inconstant in all their ways, because they are easily terrified in adversity and entangled in prosperity.

VERS. 15.-- *To them that are of a dissolute heart,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] He still teaches that error is to be avoided, etc., *as far as* to these, who do not acquiesce in the truth but believe iniquity, wrath and indignation, etc.

VERS. 17.-- *To look upon,* etc. Although God looks upon all things at every time, yet he is then said to look upon [1187C] when he is discerned to approve or to disapprove something.

VERS. 18.-- *They that fear the Lord will not be incredulous,* etc. He treats alternately of the love and the affection of God, *because the fear of the Lord is holy, enduring for ever and ever [n: (Psal. XVIII)]*, *and every one that loveth is born of God, and knoweth God [n: (I Joan. IV)]*. But he who fears God, and loves, and believes the Scriptures, keeps the precepts of God by working them, and always by meditating seeks the things that are well pleasing to him: he shall therefore be filled with the wisdom and the charity of God. *For the end of the commandment is charity, and he that loveth his neighbour hath fulfilled the law.*

VERS. 20.-- *They that fear the Lord will prepare,* etc. Happy the soul which daily cleanses its heart that it may receive God as its indweller; the possessor of him lacks no good thing, because he has within himself the author of all good things. [1187D] And because for this the keeping of the commandments is necessary, and the patience of good work, by which one comes to the knowledge of the truth, there follows: *They that fear the Lord keep his commandments,* etc. The just man is first of all his own accuser. For as a reward remains for humility, so a punishment remains for pride; whence John: *If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves [n: (II Joan. I)]*. He who is truly wise is a true keeper of justice, because wisdom dictates the rule of justice.

## CHAPTER III.

VERS. 2.-- *The judgment of the father.* Of God, *of whom all fatherhood in heaven and on earth.* Because from him are all things. He loves the things which he has made, and loves that they should abide in him in whom they were made; and whoever hears his judgment, and does his precepts, [1188A] shall be saved: whose commandment it is that reverence be shown also to a temporal father and mother; whence: *Honour thy father [n: (Deut. V)]*, etc.; whence there follows: *He that honoureth his father.* He for whom he appointed God as his honour ought not to be dishonoured by his sons: because God will by his judgment search out how his precept is kept.

VERS. 4.-- *He that loveth.* He, namely, who keeps the commandments and abstains from sins, and yet does not cease to pray for transgressors, because he knows that a merciful judge hears prayers at every time.

VERS. 6.-- *In the children.* [n: (RAB.)] In offspring or in disciples, etc., *as far as* to honour parents is the first commandment with a promise.

[1188B]VERS. 9.-- *In work and word,* not in the womb, namely, whence it is shown that the spiritual father also is most worthy of honour; whence Paul: *Through the Gospel I have begotten you [n: (I Cor. IV)]*. And elsewhere: *Let the priests that rule well be esteemed worthy of double honour, especially they who labour in doctrine and word [n: (I Tim. V)]*. [var: Vulg. *in verbo et doctrina*, in the reverse order]

VERS. 11.-- *The blessing of the father,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] The patriarchs blessed their sons, etc., *as far as* they most savagely tore the mockers.

VERS. 15.-- *Alms.* Namely, that which blots out sin. For the victim which is offered for sin is called sin. And he who has mercy on his parents, or on the rest of the poor, shall receive the reward of justice, absolved from his sins. *Blessed are the merciful, for [n: (Matth. V)]*, etc. And elsewhere: *He lendeth to the Lord that hath mercy on the poor.* [1188C] [n: (Prov. XIX)]. Hence Daniel to Nabuchodonosor: *Let my counsel, O king, be pleasing to thee: redeem thou thy sins with alms, and thy iniquities with works of mercy to the poor [n: (Dan. IV)]*, if perhaps God may forgive thy offences. Hence the Lord says: *Give alms, and all things are clean unto you [n: (Luc. XI)]*.

VERS. 19.-- *Son, in meekness.* Meekness and humility bring forth grace; pride and rage bring forth ruin; whence: *Learn of me, because I am meek and humble of heart [n: (Matth. XI)]*, etc. And elsewhere: *He that exalteth himself shall be humbled [n: (Luc. XIV)]*, etc.

VERS. 21.-- *The greater thou art,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] Above he taught meekness, etc., *as far as* it is enough for a man to think devoutly upon, and to fulfil in work, those things which God has commanded.

[1188D]VERS. 24.-- *In superfluous things,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] That is, that thou search not superfluously, etc., *as far as* disputing they fall into errors, and depart from the truth.

VERS. 27.-- *A hard heart.* Because *according to thy hardness thou treasurest up to thyself wrath in the day of judgment [n: (Rom. II)]*. [var: Vulg. *in die irae*, "in the day of wrath"]

VERS. 28.-- *A heart going in.* Which takes no care, nor is at pains to avoid, and because it loves those things which lead to destruction, such as heresies and profane novelties; whence there follows: *A heart that goeth two ways shall not have success,* etc.



## CHAPTER IV.

VERS. 1.-- *Son, the alms of the poor,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] How much alms avails, etc., *as far as* he who from the heart rebukes in words or in deeds.

[1189A]VERS. 3.-- *The heart of the needy,* etc. Alms is not to be put off, when the means of giving is at hand; whence: *Say not to thy friend: Go, and come again, when thou canst give at once [n: (Prov. III)]*. [var: Vulg. *cras dabo tibi: cum statim possis dare*] And elsewhere: *He that despiseth his neighbour sinneth: he that hath mercy on the poor shall be blessed [n: (Ibid. XIV)]*. And alms is to be done not out of necessity, *for God loveth a cheerful giver [n: (I Cor. IX)]*. And elsewhere: The poor widow cast more than all into the treasury, because God does not weigh the quantity of the gift, but the devotion of the heart.

VERS. 5.-- *Turn not away from the needy,* etc. The poor man is not to be exasperated by anger, but to be appeased by gentle speech, *for the anger of man worketh not the justice of God [n: (Jac. I)]*. And, *He that stoppeth his ear at the cry of the poor shall cry, and the Lord shall not hear him [n: (Prov. XXI)]*. [var: Vulg. *aurem suam … et ipse clamabit, et non exaudietur*] [1189B] For he who is able to give ought to give: because a hidden gift quenches anger, and a present in the bosom quenches the greatest indignation. But he who is not able, a good word is better for him than the best gift. *But he that hath the substance of the world, and shall see his brother in need, and shall shut up his bowels from him, how doth the charity of God abide in him? [n: (I Joan. III.)]* [var: Vulg. *substantiam hujus mundi … necessitatem habere*] For faith, if it have not works, is dead. Let us not therefore love in tongue and in word, but in deed and in truth.

VERS. 7.-- *To the congregation of the poor.* In these things meekness and humility are commended, because meekness despises no one, humility subjects itself to all. And it becomes a Christian to be affable and gentle toward his equals and inferiors, and humble toward his elders; whence: *Lord, my heart is not exalted, neither [1189C] are my eyes lofty [n: (Psal. CXXX)]*.

VERS. 9.-- *Deliver,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] As he said that bounty toward the poor is alms, so he shows that the deliverance of one unjustly oppressed is mercy; whence, *Deliver them that are led to death.*

VERS. 10.-- *In judging.* [n: (RAB.)] No kind of alms, etc., *as far as* so also the solace of a husband to a widow.

VERS. 13.-- *And they that watch,* etc. *Blessed is the man that heareth me, and that watcheth before my doors daily, and waiteth at the posts of my door [n: (Prov. VIII)]*. And by the doors thou canst, he understands the Scriptures and their teachers.

VERS. 15.-- *They that serve,* etc. He who loves him that [1189D] begot will love him that is born of God, and whom the Father loves, the Son loves; whence: He that loveth me shall be loved by my Father, and I will love him. But because *the proof of love is the showing of the work,* there follows: *He that heareth her shall judge the nations.* Whence: *When the Son of man shall sit on the seat of his majesty, you also shall sit on twelve seats, judging the twelve tribes of Israel [n: (Matth. XIX)]*.

VERS. 19.-- *Fear and dread,* etc. Wisdom dwelling within directs works; in various temptations it prepares a man, by exercising and proving him, for the joys of the life to come; which is confirmed by this sentence: *Fear and dread and proving,* etc. Because tribulation works patience, and patience trial, and trial hope, [1190A] which confoundeth not, because the charity of God is poured forth in the saints through the Holy Spirit.

VERS. 23.-- *Son, keep the time,* etc. Above he commended the gift of wisdom; now he shows the deed of wisdom herself. For whoever keeps the precepts of wisdom is wary in the change of times, and does not forsake the way of justice in the time of persecution and of distress. Therefore wisdom exhorts her sons to keep the time, because there is a time for everything under heaven: and there is a time of war, and a time of peace.

VERS. 28.-- *Hide not thy wisdom,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] Wisdom is not to be hidden from those who are willing to hear. For he that hideth up corn shall be cursed among the people, but a blessing is upon the head of them that sell; whence: *Do business, till I come [n: (Luc. XIX)]*. [var: Vulg. *Negotiamini*, "trade ye"]

[1190B]VERS. 30.-- *Contradict not.* Obedience is due to superiors, if they agree with truth and justice, and not otherwise; but for right faith and true religion, in which is the soul's salvation, one must contend; whence: *If thy eye scandalize thee, pluck it out and cast it from thee [n: (Matth. V)]*. And, *If any man will come after me, let him deny [n: (Luc. IX)]*, etc.

VERS. 34.-- *Be not hasty in thy tongue.* [n: (RAB.)] Death and life, etc., *as far as* it is written: *The kingdom of God is not in speech, but in power [n: (I Cor. IV)]*.

VERS. 35.-- *Be not as a lion.* In the Church there are heretics like lions, who by the glibness of the tongue lead astray the hearts of the innocent, and by the insolence of their manners trouble the meekness of the simple.

## CHAPTER V.

[1190C]VERS. 11.-- *Winnow not thyself,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] He reproves levity, etc., *as far as* he shows that the doubleness of their teaching, in which they now put forward true things and now false, proves them to be sinners.

VERS. 13.-- *Be meek.* It is good to hear meekly, and to receive the word of truth, and to utter it modestly and prudently; whence: *Let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak and slow to anger. [n: (Jac. I)]*. And a little after: *With meekness receive the ingrafted word, which is able to save your souls [n: (Ibid.)]* In the Proverbs also it is said: *Hast thou seen a man swift to speak [sic: loquendeum]? folly is rather to be looked for than his correction [n: (Prov. XXIX)]*. [var: Vulg. *illius correptio*, "his reproof"]



## CHAPTER VI.

[1190D]VERS. 1.-- *Be ye not made,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] He shows the force of true charity, etc., *as far as* his own strength shall be dashed to pieces.

VERS. 4.-- *Wicked.* Upon a good will there follows the fruit of good work, and upon a malicious mind no prosperity at all. For if charity be lacking, in vain dost thou spend labour upon virtue; whence: *He that offendeth in one point is become guilty of all [n: (Jac. II)]*. And, *from him that hath not, even that which he hath shall be taken away from him [n: (Luc. XIX)]*.

VERS. 6.-- *Let many be at peace with thee,* etc. Peace is to be kept with all, so far as our frailty allows, but not counsel with many, because it is written: *They are called merciful men, but who shall find a faithful man? [n: (Prov. XX.)]*

[1191A]VERS. 7.-- *If thou wouldst get a friend,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] Setting forth false friends under various kinds, he comes at last to the true friend: because many profess themselves friends in prosperity, and appear enemies in adversity. Whence: *If he shall humble himself against thee,* etc.

VERS. 13.-- *Take heed.* [n: (RAB.)] That is, have discernment, etc., *as far as: Now I beseech you, brethren, that you mark them who make dissensions and offences [n: (Rom. XVI)]*.

VERS. 14.-- *A strong friend.* [var: Vulg. *Amicus fidelis protectio fortis*, "a faithful friend is a strong defence"] A friend is a sharer of love, to whom thou shouldst so join thy mind that out of two there be made one; to whom thou shouldst entrust thyself as to thyself; from whom thou shouldst fear nothing, and of whom thou shouldst ask nothing dishonourable. For friendship is not a thing of tribute, but full of comeliness; whence: *You are my friends, if you do the things that I command [1191B] you [n: (Joan. XV)]*, etc. The Lord has given us a pattern of friendship for us to follow: that we do the friend's will, that we open our secrets to him, and he to us; whence: *But I have called you friends, because all things whatsoever I have heard of my Father, I have made known to you [n: (Ibid.)]*.

VERS. 16.-- *A faithful friend.* According to God, namely. He treats with his friend of the things necessary for the medicine of eternal life and of immortality: whence Cicero says that friendship cannot be except among good men, and that friendship ought to be free, and inclined toward every happiness.

VERS. 17.-- *He that feareth the Lord.* [var: Vulg. *Qui timet Deum*] [n: (RAB.)] The full and perfect grace of friendship, etc., *as far as* that thou mayest believe thyself about to depart from this world every day.

VERS. 27.-- *With all thy mind.* [n: (RAB.)] With the heart, not [1191C] with the body, must one approach wisdom, etc., *as far as* the perception of the truth; whence: *Now this is eternal life, that they may know thee, the only true God [n: (Joan. XVII.)]*, etc. [var: Vulg. *solum Deum verum*, "the only God, true"]

VERS. 33.-- *Son, if thou wilt attend.* Wisdom admonishes us to meditate assiduously upon the divine law. First she exhorts us to learn; afterward, to apply the soul to this; then, to incline; and lastly, to bring diligence to the hearing. For thus does wisdom promise that a man shall be wise. For it is necessary that he who desires the knowledge of true wisdom, which is Christ, should first humbly subject himself to catholic teachers, and all the affections of his soul to their discipline. Thereafter, turning the intention of his heart away from every crooked desire, let him diligently bring it to the hearing of the word of God, and let him beware [1191D] that he spend his meditation of the law not for the wages of earthly things, nor of human praise, but for the love of that good itself, so that he may receive the fruit of true wisdom.

VERS. 35.-- *In the multitude.* As if to say: Be not wise in thine own eyes. Trust not thine own wit; the arrogance of pride has above all supplanted heretics.

VERS. 38.-- *Have thy thought upon the precepts.* [n: (RAB.)] Deservedly is it given to him, etc., *as far as* and he assiduously meditates the law and fulfils it in work.

## CHAPTER VII.

*Thou shalt not reap them sevenfold.* [n: (RAB.)] Perfect vengeance, etc., *as far as He taketh seven other spirits more wicked than himself [n: (Luc. XI)]*.

[1192A]VERS. 4.-- *Nor of the king a chair of honour.* He cannot exercise the work of just governance who has neglected the sentence of true godliness; whence: *The kings of the Gentiles lord it over them; but you not so: but he that is the greater among you, let him become as the lesser [n: (Luc. XXII)]*.

VERS. 5.-- *For he is the searcher.* No presumption is more destructive than to be proud of one's own justice or knowledge; whence: *There is not a man upon earth that doeth good, and sinneth not [n: (Eccl. VII)]*. [var: Vulg. *Non est enim homo justus in terra*] And elsewhere: *Hast thou seen a man to seem wise to himself, and the fool hath more hope than he [n: (Prov. XXVI)]*. [var: Vulg. *magis illo spem habebit insipiens*]

VERS. 6.-- *Seek not to be made a judge, unless thou be strong enough.* Every man ought to weigh his own powers, and to take up the care of others in proportion to the measure of his strength: lest, while he delights in a place of glory, he become to his subjects the author of ruin; and [1192B] lest he who is weighed down by the burden of his own faults wish to be made a judge of other men's.

VERS. 7.-- *Sin not against the multitude.* He who is strong in reason, and prevails by the power of free choice, let him not sin through the insolence of his subjects, but let him steadfastly resist another's wickedness: nor let him think that he sins with impunity if he acquiesces in the will of the many; whence: *And not only they that do them, but they that consent to him that doeth them [n: (Rom. I.)]*, etc.

VERS. 13.-- *Love not a lie.* [var: Vulg. *arare*, "to plough a lie"] Every lie is evil; and to bring scandal upon our neighbours is destructive.
